synopsis: NIH’s review model asks whether work should be done, whether it can be done well, and whether the necessary expertise and resources are in place; the glossary repeats this planning framework [f9833, f16461]. The Simplified Review Framework notice NOT-OD-24-010 was released on 19 October 2023 and applies to due dates on or after 25 January 2025, while reviewer materials updated through September 2026 reinforce structured evaluation rather than enthusiasm [f9829, f9835]. For the heavy off-road collision mitigation validation plan, the corpus recommends the NIH Approach section as a structural template, including potential problems, alternative strategies, benchmarks for success, and attention to establishing feasibility in risky early-stage work [f9978, f9979, f9834]. Structured review does not guarantee reviewer agreement: Pier and colleagues’ 2018 study found no agreement on application quality when 43 reviewers assessed the same 25 NIH applications, with Krippendorff’s alpha values all near zero [f9846, f9471]. NIH is one source for the broader skeptical-review checklist, which is practice-derived expert opinion rather than a ranking; the often-cited 1987 Cuca and McLoughlin study on NIH rejection reasons remains unverified in the corpus [f10212, f9841].
